purpose: How the AI Workflow Generator builds TRIGGER FILTERS (trigger_rules) on a Zuper-event trigger node so a workflow fires only when the entity matches (e.g. 'only HIGH-priority Repair jobs'). The per-module field list is SERVER-DRIVEN — fetch it at runtime, do not hardcode.

provenance.shape_and_field_list: Adapted from colleague repo zuper-ai-workflow/captures/trigger_filter_schema.json + docs/13-trigger-filters.md — LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-06-09 (GET /jobs/meta/filter → 65 fields = 45 default + 20 custom). This is UI-faithful (built by the advance-filter component from the meta/filter catalogue).

applies_to.EXTERNAL_WEBHOOK: NO — no trigger-level filtering. Use an if_else gate right after the trigger instead (false branch → stop_execution).
applies_to.SCHEDULE_EVENT: NO — schedule has trigger_rules_interval (timing), not entity filtering. Use if_else after the trigger.

runtime_semantics.where_stored: trigger_node.form_fields.trigger_rules.value (array). Empty array ⇒ fire on every event of that type.
runtime_semantics.evaluation: Two-phase. (1) PAYLOAD-BASED for events job.status_update and job.update_checklist — rules on status_uid/status_type/status_name matched directly against the event payload (no API call). (2) API-BASED for all other rules — POST to the module's ..._list_v2 filter API with the rules + an auto-appended module_uid CONTAINS rule, limit:1.
runtime_semantics.outcome: ≥1 record matches ⇒ workflow proceeds. 0 matches ⇒ execution status = SKIPPED (workflow does not run). API error ⇒ execution status = FAILED.
runtime_semantics.note: module_uid is appended by the backend automatically; the generator does NOT add it.

trigger_form_fields.filter_rule_operator: AND | OR — how rules combine. Flat list, NO nested groups.
trigger_form_fields.excluded_user_uids: array<user_uid> — skip events caused by these users (loop prevention)

rule_object.key: field identifier = fieldDataKey from meta/filter (e.g. 'job_category_uid', 'current_job_status.status_type', or 'cf_<uuid>' for custom)
rule_object.field_type: data type from meta/filter field.fieldType (see field_types)
rule_object.operator: one of THIS field's meta/filter field.operators[].displayValue
rule_object.displayKeyValue: human-readable echo of value (UI display; array)
rule_object.rangeKey: optional, DATE only: TODAY | LAST_7_DAYS | LAST_30_DAYS | THIS_MONTH | CUSTOM_DATE | …

field_list_source.rule: SERVER-DRIVEN per module — fetch, do not hardcode. The generator calls fetch_trigger_filters(module).
field_list_source.returns_per_field: { type, fieldDataKey, fieldType, multiSelect, fieldOptions[] (DROPDOWN/RADIO/MULTI_ITEM), operators[{displayValue}], data:{url,dataKey} (LOOKUP) }
field_list_source.includes_custom_fields: YES — per-company custom fields appear as key='cf_<uuid>', type='custom_field' (JOB returned 20).

field_types._note: ALWAYS use the field's own operators[] from meta/filter. Lists below are the typical superset.

LOOKUP.value: uid | uid[] (multiSelect); options lazy from field.data.url, value=field.data.dataKey

important_distinction_vs_if_else: Trigger filters use IS_EMPTY / IS_NOT_EMPTY and BETWEEN. The if_else NODE uses EMPTY / NOT_EMPTY (and adds string/array operators). Do NOT mix the two operator vocabularies.

value_resolution.DROPDOWN/RADIO/MULTI_ITEM: Pick option key(s) from the field's fieldOptions[] (static, in the meta/filter response).
value_resolution.LOOKUP: Resolve the human name to a UID via MCP (see mcp_resolution_map.json) — e.g. job_category_uid via list_job_categories, status_uid via list_job_statuses, assigned_to.user_uid via list_users, team_uid via list_teams. The field's data.url confirms the source; data.dataKey is the value key.
value_resolution.custom_field (cf_<uuid>): field def + options come from the same meta/filter response (or list_custom_field_definitions(module)).
value_resolution.ambiguity: If a name matches >1 record, raise a clarifying question — never guess.

special_keys.current_job_status.status_type: JOB status bucket (NEW, SCHEDULED, COMPLETED, …) — DROPDOWN. Payload-based for job.status_update.
special_keys.<module>_current_status.status_uid: nested status UID (PROJECT etc.), filtered by that module's category

option_source._purpose: Every filter field's value source is ONE of three classes. This decides whether the agent must call MCP.
option_source.STATIC_ENUM: Global, platform-fixed options — IDENTICAL for every company. Enumerated below in static_enums. The agent picks from the known set with NO MCP call.
option_source.ACCOUNT_LOOKUP: Per-company options — resolve the human name to a UID at runtime via an MCP resolver (account_lookup_resolvers). Includes custom fields.
option_source.FREE: User-supplied text / number / date — no enum, no lookup.
option_source.detection_rule: In a GET /{metaApiKey}/meta/filter field: inline `values`/`fieldOptions[]` ⇒ STATIC_ENUM (use directly); `data.url` (LOOKUP) or description '…UID from list_X' ⇒ ACCOUNT_LOOKUP; TEXT/NUMBER/DATE with neither ⇒ FREE. So the class is also detectable at runtime, not only from this catalog.

static_enums._note: Company-INDEPENDENT fixed option sets (no MCP call needed). JOB set verified live via get_module_filters 2026-06-10. `priority` is universal across modules; each module's status_type bucket is its own system enum.
static_enums.other_module_status_type: INVOICE/ESTIMATE/PROJECT/REQUEST/etc. each expose a system status_type/state enum (company-independent) via their meta/filter — treat as STATIC_ENUM; fetch once if not enumerated here. The per-company NAMED status (status_uid) is always ACCOUNT_LOOKUP.

account_lookup_resolvers._note: ACCOUNT_LOOKUP fields → the read-only MCP tool that resolves a human name to the UID (per company). See mcp_resolution_map.json + mcp_tool_policy.json (allowlist).
account_lookup_resolvers.cf_<uuid> (custom field): list_custom_field_definitions(module) for the field + its options

illustrative_field_inventory: See reference/TRIGGER_FILTERS.md for indicative per-module field tables. Those are snapshots for human reference only — the runtime authority is GET /{metaApiKey}/meta/filter (which also returns per-company custom fields).
